findings.title: .small-action button's float:right is inert now that .small-action is a flex container
findings.body: The PR adds `@include flexbox()` to `.small-action`, which makes its direct children (`.topic-avatar`, `.small-action-desc`, and the `button`) flex items. Per the flexbox spec, `float` is ignored on flex items, so the existing `button { float: right; }` no longer has any effect, and nothing replaces it (no `margin-left: auto` on the button, no `justify-content: space-between` on the container). The button that used to be pushed to the right edge of the row will now sit immediately next to the description text. The same applies to the now-dead `float: left` on `.topic-avatar` and the `clear: both` on `.small-action`. Either drop the obsolete float/clear declarations and add an explicit right-alignment mechanism (e.g. `margin-left: auto` on the button), or verify the new compact alignment is intended.

findings.title: Legacy flexbox fallbacks don't reproduce the new layout; non-flexbox browsers get a stacked header
findings.body: The new `flexbox()` mixin emits 2009-spec `display: -webkit-box` / `-moz-box`, but the layouts built on it rely on mechanisms that the 2009 box model does not support. Specifically, `.d-header .panel`'s right-alignment now depends on `margin-left: auto`, which is a no-op in the old `-webkit-box` model (that spec uses `-webkit-box-pack`), so Safari 6- and old-Gecko browsers will render the panel hugging the title instead of right-aligned. Worse, the PR removes the `float: left` on `.d-header .title` and `float: right` on `.panel` with no float fallback, and `.small-action`'s children lose their floats too; in any browser with no flexbox support at all (IE9, older Android stock browser) the header contents and small-action rows collapse into vertically stacked blocks. If those browsers are still in the support matrix, a float-based fallback or `@supports` guard is needed; if not, the dead old-spec declarations only add output CSS weight.

findings.title: -ms-align-items is not a real CSS property
findings.body: The `align-items()` mixin emits `-ms-align-items: $alignment`, but no browser has ever implemented a property with that name; Microsoft's IE10 flexbox property is `-ms-flex-align`, which the mixin already emits on the previous line. The `-ms-align-items` declaration is dead code that ships in every compiled stylesheet that uses the mixin. It should be removed so future readers don't assume it does something.

findings.title: order(2) on .extra-info-wrapper only works if it is a direct child of the header flex container
findings.body: `@include order(2)` emits flexbox `order` properties, which only apply to direct children of a flex container. The only flex container introduced in the header is `.d-header .contents`, whose direct children are `.title` and `.panel`. If `.extra-info-wrapper` is rendered inside `.title` (as the header template structures it), the `order(2)` declaration is inert and the reordering it is meant to provide never happens — while the removed `&.bullet { margin-top: 5px; }` alignment fix is genuinely lost. Confirm the element's position in the DOM; if it is nested inside `.title`, either move the flex context to `.title` or drop the order include.
